title: Escalation Playbook v2 — Severity Matrix & Triage Criteria (P0–P4 / Sev0–Sev3)
author: Dev Patel
body:
h1. Purpose
This page standardizes how Redwood Inference classifies customer-impacting issues and how Support/CS triages them before (and during) escalation. It defines:

* *Priority (P0–P4)*: customer impact and urgency used by Support/CS and Engineering.
* *Incident Severity (Sev0–Sev3)*: SRE incident classification used when an incident is declared.
* A *triage checklist* with required evidence by failure mode (5xx, timeouts, streaming disconnects, 429s, Dedicated capacity, Private SSO/networking/audit-log issues, and data integrity concerns).

This matrix applies across *Hosted API*, *Dedicated*, and *Private (VPC/on-prem)* deployments.

----

h1. Definitions (what the numbers mean)

h2. Priority (P0–P4)
Priority reflects the *customer-facing impact* and how fast we need a mitigation. Priority is assigned at intake and may change as impact is confirmed.

* *P0 — Critical outage / severe customer harm*
* *P1 — Major degradation or high-risk issue*
* *P2 — Moderate impact with workaround*
* *P3 — Minor impact / limited scope*
* *P4 — Question / request / non-urgent*

h2. Incident Severity (Sev0–Sev3)
Sev levels are used when SRE declares an incident (via incident-bot and #incidents).

* *Sev0 — Broad, business-critical outage* (multi-region or systemic, severe customer harm)
* *Sev1 — Major production incident* (single region or major subsystem, high impact)
* *Sev2 — Degradation incident* (limited blast radius, measurable impact)
* *Sev3 — Minor incident / operational event* (low impact, often handled during business hours)

h2. Mapping: Priority ↔ Incident Severity
Priority and Sev are related but not identical. *Not every P0/P1 requires declaring an incident*, but most do.

|| Support Priority || Typical Incident Severity (if incident declared) || Notes ||
| P0 | Sev0 or Sev1 | Default to incident unless clearly isolated to one customer’s misconfiguration with an immediate safe workaround. |
| P1 | Sev1 or Sev2 | May be incident depending on scope/uncertainty. If multiple customers or unknown cause, lean incident. |
| P2 | Sev2 or Sev3 | Usually not an incident unless trending upward or tied to a production change. |
| P3 | Sev3 | Typically ticket-only. |
| P4 | N/A | No incident. |

*Rule of thumb:* If Support cannot confidently answer “is this only this customer?” within ~30 minutes for a high-impact symptom, engage SRE and consider incident declaration.

----

h1. Severity matrix (P0–P4) with concrete examples
Use the table below to assign initial Priority. If you’re between two levels, choose the higher Priority and downgrade later.

|| Priority || Customer impact definition || Examples (LLM inference + platform) || Required action / engagement ||
| *P0* | *Production outage or safety/compliance critical issue.* Customer cannot use core service or is experiencing severe harm. No validated workaround (or workaround unacceptable). | *Hosted/Dedicated:* sustained 5xx spike (e.g., >5% requests failing for 10+ min) for a region/model; widespread timeouts (p95 latency exceeds customer timeout leading to broad failures); streaming disconnects affecting a large fraction of sessions; routing/scheduler failure causing request drops.  *Private:* SSO outage preventing all user access; control plane unavailable; audit logs not generating for regulated customer (confirmed gap); critical networking break (ingress/egress blocked) after Redwood change. *Security:* suspected credential compromise, data exposure, cross-tenant leak, signing key/KMS incident. | *Immediately page SRE oncall* (and Security oncall if security indicators). Start incident process if scope is unclear or >1 customer suspected. Provide customer update within SLA for tier (see SLA page). |
| *P1* | *Major degradation or high-risk issue.* Significant subset of traffic/users impacted; or one high-tier customer severely impacted with no immediate safe mitigation; or issue likely to become P0. | Elevated 5xx or timeouts localized to single region/model version (e.g., pinned model in eu-west) with partial failover possible; Dedicated capacity shortfall causing sustained queueing/latency spikes during peak hours; streaming disconnects isolated to a POP/edge path; Private: SAML login works for some users but fails for a major group after IdP change, or token validation intermittently fails; audit-log delays >2 hours for compliance-bound customer. | Engage SRE within the Engineering engagement SLA. Consider incident if trending or unknown cause. Identify and validate safe workaround (region failover, model rollback, retry guidance, config change). |
| *P2* | *Moderate impact with workaround available.* Customer can operate with degraded experience or a validated mitigation. | Intermittent timeouts with a known client-side retry + timeout tuning workaround; 429s due to quota/rate limits with clear remediation (burst settings, backoff, quota increase workflow); Dedicated: short-lived latency spikes mitigated by scaling or routing policy change; Private: SSO failure limited to one integration path (e.g., one IdP app) with a documented fix. | Support-led mitigation using Known Issues pages and validated playbooks. Escalate to Engineering if workaround fails, scope expands, or metrics indicate a platform regression. |
| *P3* | *Minor impact / limited blast radius.* Non-blocking defect, docs issue, usability problem, or small set of requests affected. | Single endpoint nuance; minor SDK error message confusion; sporadic streaming disconnects resolved by reconnect; one-off 5xx for a single request id; performance question where service is within published targets. | Handle via standard ticket workflow. Create bug/task if needed. No paging. |
| *P4* | *No immediate impact / informational.* Questions, how-to, feature requests, planned maintenance questions. | “How do quotas work?”, “Can we pin a model version?”, “What is the recommended timeout?”, “How do we set up Private SSO?” | Provide guidance, link docs, schedule follow-up. |

Notes:
* Customer tier (*self-serve vs Dedicated vs Private/Enterprise*) affects *SLA and comms cadence*, not the Priority definition. Do not inflate Priority solely due to account size; instead ensure the correct SLA is applied.
* For Dedicated/Private accounts, confirm whether the impact is *single-tenant* (their deployment only) vs a *shared control-plane / hosted service* issue.

----

h1. Triage criteria: what to check before escalating
The goal is to (a) correctly classify severity, (b) collect the minimum evidence Engineering/SRE needs, and (c) apply validated workarounds quickly.

h2. Triage checklist (run top-to-bottom)
1) *Confirm impact and scope*
   * Who is affected? (one user, one org, multiple orgs)
   * Which deployment mode? (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
   * Region(s), model(s), and whether model version is pinned
   * Time window (start time, ongoing vs resolved)

2) *Confirm symptom category*
   * 5xx errors
   * Timeouts / high latency
   * Streaming disconnects (SSE/websocket)
   * 429 throttling / quota
   * Auth/SSO/access
   * Data integrity (wrong tenant data, wrong outputs due to misrouting, missing audit logs)

3) *Collect required identifiers (do not escalate without these unless P0)*
   * *Request IDs* (at least 3 representative IDs spanning the failure window)
   * *Timestamps with timezone* for each request id
   * *Org/project id* (internal) and customer-facing org name
   * *SDK + version* or raw HTTP details
   * *Endpoint* (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank), streaming on/off
   * *Model name + version* (and quantization/profile if relevant)
   * *Region* and *base URL*

4) *Check known issues first (5 minutes max)*
   * Search: *Known Issues & Workarounds* index
   * If match found, use the validated workaround and link the KB page in the ticket.

5) *Determine if this is customer configuration vs platform*
   * Look for: recent customer deployment/config changes, new traffic launch, changed timeouts, IdP changes (Private SSO), new egress allowlists.
   * Look for: correlated metrics in Console (error rate, latency), other tickets, #support/#incidents chatter.

6) *Apply safe first mitigations (if applicable and validated)*
   * Client retry/backoff for 429/timeouts
   * Increase client timeout for streaming where appropriate
   * Region failover hints (Hosted) if the customer can tolerate
   * Model rollback/unpin guidance if a pinned version is implicated
   * Dedicated: temporary autoscaling/routing policy adjustments per runbook

7) *Escalate using the correct path*
   * SRE oncall for suspected platform/regional/runtime issues
   * Runtime/Platform engineering if clearly in their component with reproducible evidence
   * Private Deployments + Security for SSO/audit-log/compliance concerns

8) *Set comms cadence and next update time*
   * Always give a timestamp for next update (“Next update by 14:30 PT”).
   * If incident declared, mirror updates per Support–Incident comms alignment doc.

9) *Keep the evidence trail clean*
   * Link: Jira ticket, Slack thread, dashboards, incident channel, GitHub PR (if any).
   * Use restricted handling if customer-sensitive (Private/enterprise logs, security-related content).

10) *Re-evaluate Priority*
   * Upgrade if scope expands or workaround fails.
   * Downgrade once mitigation is confirmed and stable.

----

h1. Failure-mode specific triage requirements
Use the relevant section below to avoid back-and-forth with SRE/Engineering.

h2. 5xx errors (500/502/503/504)
Minimum evidence to collect:
* 3–10 *request IDs* with timestamps
* Exact *HTTP status codes* and any error body fields
* Region + model + endpoint
* Whether streaming was enabled
* Any correlation with a deploy/rollout window (ask SRE if unsure)

Quick checks:
* Is the error correlated to a single region or model version (pinned)?
* Is it only one customer project (misuse, bad auth token, malformed payload) or multiple?

Escalation triggers:
* P0 if >5% sustained failures for a region/model (10+ minutes) or multiple enterprise customers impacted.
* P1 if isolated but high-impact to one major customer and no immediate workaround.

h2. Timeouts / latency spikes
Minimum evidence to collect:
* Client timeout setting (seconds)
* p50/p95 observed latency from customer (if they have) + request IDs
* Prompt/context length and max_tokens (approximate is fine)
* Whether requests are streaming (streaming often “looks” slower but should produce tokens early)

Quick checks:
* Confirm customer is not using an unrealistically low timeout for their output length.
* Ask if they changed prompt size or concurrency.

Escalation triggers:
* P0 if broad timeouts begin suddenly across many customers/regions.
* P1 if single region/model shows sustained p95 regression relative to baseline.

h2. Streaming disconnects (SSE)
Minimum evidence to collect:
* Are disconnects happening before first token or mid-stream?
* Client language + SDK version
* Network path details if available (corporate proxy, mobile networks, long-lived connections)
* Request IDs and timestamps

Validated mitigations (safe to share):
* Use idempotency/retry strategy appropriate for streaming (see streaming reconnect KB page).
* Ensure client handles intermittent disconnects by reconnecting and resuming at the application layer.

Escalation triggers:
* P0 if disconnect rate spikes broadly (multiple customers) or correlates with edge/runtime change.
* P1 if confined to a major region/PoP or enterprise account with no viable reconnect strategy.

h2. 429 throttling / quota
Minimum evidence to collect:
* Exact 429 error payload fields (limit, remaining, reset if provided)
* Concurrency pattern (bursts vs steady state)
* Which project/org key is used

Quick checks:
* Confirm the customer understands *rate limit vs quota*.
* Validate whether this is expected based on plan limits and recent traffic change.

Validated mitigations:
* Exponential backoff with jitter; avoid synchronized retries.
* Use client-side concurrency limits.
* Request quota increase or discuss Dedicated if sustained throughput required.

Escalation triggers:
* P1 if 429s appear inconsistent with configured limits (possible misconfiguration/bug).
* P0 only if 429s are caused by a platform regression affecting many customers unexpectedly.

h2. Dedicated capacity shortfalls / noisy neighbor symptoms
Minimum evidence to collect:
* Dedicated cluster name / tenant identifier (internal)
* Time window and whether issue aligns with peak load
* Observed queueing metrics if available (Support can link Dedicated dashboards if provisioned)

Quick checks:
* Has workload concurrency increased? Any new job types (long context, high max_tokens)?
* Is autoscaling enabled and correctly configured?

Escalation triggers:
* P1 if sustained latency spikes prevent operation during business-critical periods.
* P2 if workaround exists (temporary scaling, routing policy adjustment) and can be applied quickly.

h2. Private: SSO/SAML/OIDC access issues
Minimum evidence to collect (handle as *restricted* if enterprise/private):
* Private deployment version + installer version (if on-prem)
* IdP type (Okta/AzureAD/etc), recent IdP change details
* SAML/OIDC error codes (redact secrets), affected user count
* Whether this blocks *all users* or a subset

Escalation triggers:
* P0 if all users cannot access the system in production.
* P1 if subset blocked but business-critical.

Security involvement:
* Engage Security escalation owner if there is any sign of token validation bypass, unexpected role mapping, or suspicious auth events.

h2. Data integrity / cross-tenant / compliance (audit logs)
Treat these as high-risk even if volume appears low.

Minimum evidence to collect:
* Exact description of suspected issue (what data, which tenant, what was observed)
* Request IDs, timestamps, and affected resources
* Whether any PII/regulated data may be involved

Immediate actions:
* Mark ticket *restricted*.
* Page Security oncall for suspected exposure/cross-tenant access.

Priority guidance:
* Suspected data exposure or cross-tenant leak: *P0*.
* Confirmed audit-log gaps for compliance-bound Private customer: *P0/P1* depending on scope and duration.

----

h1. “Is this an incident?” criteria (Support → SRE alignment)
Declare an incident (or ask SRE to declare) when any of the following are true:

* Multiple customers/orgs impacted and the cause is not immediately known.
* Region-wide error/timeout regression is detected or suspected.
* There is a clear production regression tied to a deploy/rollout.
* Security/compliance risk is present (suspected exposure, auth bypass, missing audit logs for regulated environments).
* Support is receiving rapid inbound volume indicating a broad issue.

If none of the above are true and the issue is clearly isolated to one customer configuration with a validated workaround, use ticket escalation without incident.

----

h1. Appendix: examples to calibrate classification

*Example A — Hosted, eu-west pinned model 5xx*
* Symptom: 8% 5xx for model X version v3 in eu-west, only for customers with pinned version.
* Classification: *P1* (potential *Sev1/Sev2* if incident declared).
* Action: Engage SRE + Runtime; propose rollback/unpin mitigation; customer update cadence per tier.

*Example B — Self-serve 429s after product launch*
* Symptom: sudden 429s after increasing concurrency 10×.
* Classification: *P2* if limits match plan and mitigation exists (backoff + quota review).
* Action: Use 429 KB page; confirm project limits; no paging unless inconsistent with configuration.

*Example C — Private SSO outage after IdP change*
* Symptom: all users locked out post-IdP change; customer is regulated.
* Classification: *P0*.
* Action: Restricted handling; escalate Private Deployments + Security; consider incident depending on whether issue is in Redwood Private stack vs customer IdP misconfig.

*Example D — Streaming disconnects in us-east for multiple enterprise accounts*
* Symptom: multiple tickets reporting mid-stream disconnects; started after edge rollout.
* Classification: *P0/P1* depending on breadth; likely incident.
* Action: Page SRE; link request ids; apply reconnect workaround guidance; update customers with next update time.
